name: NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE · मॅचिंग सेंटर
one_line: The festive season run as Naira's own Matching Centre: twelve posts, twelve shades, each one matching a single piece to an outfit, an evening or a person, with the swatch, the shade tag and the measuring tape of the couture house Naira began as.
big_idea:
Every Indian town has a matching centre: the shop where a saree goes in and comes out with its blouse piece, its fall and its petticoat, matched by eye under a tube light. Every woman of 35 to 54 has stood at that counter, and every one of them still matches: the jewellery to the Karwa Chauth red, the Paithani to Padwa, five outfits to five wedding functions, a gift to what her mother already wears. Naira is the one demi-fine brand that really is a couture house (Nashik, made to measure, swatches and tapes on the table), so this season it opens a matching centre. ONE organising idea a stranger can name in three seconds: 'it's a matching centre; every tile is a fabric shade with a piece matched to it.'

How the grid carries it. (1) THE GRID IS A SHADE CARD: each of the twelve tiles is a full-bleed fabric colour (blush, plum, ivory, red room, lilac, bottle green, pale sage, Paithani purple, apricot, lac, tulsi sage, lac), named on a shade tag as SHADE N° 01 to N° 12, so the profile itself reads as the season's shade card. (2) THE SIGNBOARD LOCKUP, a painted shop board with the real NAIRA wordmark over MATCHING CENTRE and मॅचिंग सेंटर (the way Maharashtra's shop boards write the English word), opens the run at bottom-right (P1, 'open for the season') and closes it at top-left (P12, 'GUEST ORDERS UNDERTAKEN.'), so the two loudest tiles sit on the grid's long diagonal like PTAT's MILNI key art. (3) THE SHADE TAG, a small ivory hang-tag with a colour chip, the shade number and 'MATCHED TO ...', hangs on a gold thread from the piece: it is Naira's equivalent of the MILNI hand-and-marigold lockup, the one object that repeats so twelve different constructions read as one campaign (it hangs on nine covers; the other three carry their shade number on the counter's own paper: the order slip, the shade card, the programme). (4) Four named series, each with its own paper object from the counter: THE MATCH (one piece, one occasion), SHADE CARD (every colour a piece comes in), माप · THE MEASUREMENTS (the tailor's order slip and tape: exact facts, told straight) and THE SAMPLE BLOUSE (matching for someone who won't say what she wants). (5) The value checkerboard of the existing LAC / flower / BONE row is carried up all four new rows (light-dark-light over dark-light-dark), and the top row returns to lac oxblood at both ends, so the new season grows out of the last one instead of sitting on it.

Why it resolves the brief's tension. It is maximal in idea and system (an Indian vernacular institution, a multi-script signboard, a recurring lockup, named series, an index carousel, illustrated objects, cut-outs on fabric) and premium in execution (real product photography and cut-outs only, letterpress-quiet type in Velista and Cormorant, raw-silk texture, gold hairlines, one piece per frame, no stickers, no stamps, no offers on the art). The matching centre is also a working service, not just a metaphor: the site already promises 'Tell us who it is for and your budget. We will send back three options with photographs.' The feed turns that into the counter: send a photo of the outfit on WhatsApp and get three matches back. And it sells the thing the data says the business needs: matched sets (BUY2 / BUY3 baskets), Edition Two's new stone and metal choices, and ruby.
why_it_fits:
BRAND: Naira is 'a couture house first, so our jewellery gets styled where the thread is' (Up Close plan) and the site's own story is the Nashik studio that makes outfits to measure; no Indian demi-fine competitor can stand at a fabric counter honestly, Naira can. It uses only the brand's own tools: the kit wordmark (once, on the signboard only), the blush flower as the tag's maker's mark, Velista caps + lowercase Cormorant turn + Jost, the house numbering (N° 01 ... N° 12), the bracketed material kicker, sharp corners, and the brand's existing colour families (identity blush, the Lilac / Sage / Apricot edition grounds, exhibition bottle green, the Lac & Bone oxblood). The deck florals appear the way the owner likes them, as printed fabric (tulip georgette, sprig organza), never stuck on.
DATA: (a) The formula that sells is one piece + one everyday Indian object + one witty Indian line + one exact fact ('Anaar, pre-peeled.' = ₹335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52, best ad ever); here the everyday object is the matching centre's own kit (swatch, slip, tape, sieve, kandil, sample blouse) and every tile carries one exact fact (25 mm, 36 cm, 15 to 19 cm, ruby-red cubic zirconia, 18k gold tone plated). (b) Ruby is the hero stone (Ruby 8 of 13 Baguette Tennis Bracelets since 16 Oct; huggies sold ruby 3 of 3) and leads the key art and the closing tile. (c) Edition Two had the account's best week (19 to 24 Oct: 34 purchases, ₹854 each) and its story is choice of stone and metal: a shade card is the native frame. (d) 69% of orders are one piece and break-even needs bigger baskets: matching sets (the ruby set ₹5,198, the Nocturne trio, five functions) make BUY2/BUY3 the natural next step. (e) Buyers are women 35 to 54 (64% of purchases), Maharashtra 46% (Mumbai + Nashik): the matching centre, मॅचिंग सेंटर, Paithani, Padwa, Bhaubeej, the akash kandil and Tulsi Vivah are their world; the multi-script signboard slide is drawn from where the parcels actually went (Maharashtra, Delhi, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana). (f) 84% of attributed purchases came from IG feed and stories stills: 6 carousels + 4 singles, 2 reels for reach. (g) Sunday noon and Fri/Sun 18:00 to 21:00 IST carry the orders; the Sunday-noon and Friday-evening slots hold the gift guide, Dhanteras, Diwali, the wedding programme, the necklace proof and the ruby set. (h) The grid has been silent 76 days while Meta sent ~₹2.07 lakh of traffic to it: P1 is a relaunch, so it opens like a shop opening.
OWNER TASTE: Indian everyday-object wit with restraint (the 10/10 caption-doc lines were childhood objects told straight; here: the moon is always late, the sample blouse, 'kisne diya? maine.', guest orders undertaken); lilac and purple (three violet tiles); moody night grounds (plum, red room, lac, bottle green, Paithani purple); clean plates and chic minimal still life (one piece per frame, lots of field); exact facts and honest corrections ('IS IT GOLD?' answered on the slip, 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald'). It avoids everything she sent back: no black, no sand or beige grounds, no cool light, no orange gold, no sticker/stamp/postmark soup, no stuck-on florals, no grand copy, no discount art, no faces on product tiles, no lyrics, no spice props, nothing that reads AI-made (AI is used only for three plain textile textures).
REFERENCE: it takes PTAT's system, not its look. MILNI lockup on every event tile -> the shade tag on every tile and the signboard at both ends; the multi-script MILNI signboard -> मॅचिंग सेंटर in five scripts (P1 slide 4); the steel tray 'Accessory Guide vol 1' -> SHADE CARD vol 1 and vol 2; the [01]-[04] index with cut-outs -> THE PROGRAMME [01]-[05] and THE SAMPLE BLOUSE [01]-[04]; the drawn wardrobe framing a real photo -> the drawn blouse, kandil, sieve and tulsi around real product; script + caps -> Velista + Cormorant italic; one vernacular idiom per tile; big colour fields; a checkerboard of weight in every row.

grid_system.type_system: Three brand roles + one script, nothing else. (1) DISPLAY: Velista 400 (FEED/kit/fonts/Velista.woff2), CAPS ONLY, letter-spacing 0.03em, line-height 0.98, balanced wrap. Glyph limits: A-Z 0-9 . , ; : ! ? & ' " - ( ) @ # % / only: NO ₹, NO ·, NO °, NO accented letters (never set RIVIÈRE, PAVÉ or N° in Velista; those go in Jost). Grid-read words >= 88px (P9's '36 CM.' 200px). (2) TURN: Cormorant Garamond italic 400 (kit VF), lowercase, 40-56px, line-height 1.12, ends with a full stop; this is the 'script' half of the PTAT script + caps pairing. (3) SUPPORT: Jost (kit VF): eyebrows and labels Jost 500 caps 18-26px tracking 0.24-0.32em; support copy Jost 400 22-26px tracking 0.04em; prices always Jost 500 with font-family 'Jost','Poppins' so ₹ falls back to Poppins (kit). Max per slide: one eyebrow + two Jost support lines. (4) SCRIPT: Tiro Devanagari Marathi 400 (kit) for मॅचिंग सेंटर, माप, शुभ दीपावली, मैचिंग सेंटर, 40-64px, never more than one Devanagari line per tile except P1 slide 4. P1 slide 4 only adds Tiro Kannada, Tiro Tamil and Tiro Telugu from Google Fonts (css2?family=Tiro+Kannada|Tiro+Tamil|Tiro+Telugu) and must be glyph-checked by a native reader of each script before posting. No Kalam, Rozha, Yatra, Playfair or DM Serif anywhere. WORDMARK: kit/naira-wordmark-cream-blush.svg (P1 board) and kit/naira-wordmark-ink-blush.svg (P12 board) only; never typed, never twice in a frame; photos of the box lid count as the frame's one wordmark. Punctuation: no em dashes, no exclamation marks, no emoji; middot only in Jost metadata lines.

posts.concept: The relaunch after 76 silent days, staged as a shop opening: a painted signboard, NAIRA / MATCHING CENTRE / मॅचिंग सेंटर, above a fan of fabric swatches, the ruby baguette bracelet laid on the red one and tagged SHADE N° 01, MATCHED TO THE RED. The joke is the institution itself: every reader has stood at a matching centre counter, and a couture house opening one for its jewellery is both true and funny. The carousel then explains the counter like PTAT's key art explains MILNI: what a matching centre is, how this one works (bring the outfit, we match the shade, it leaves in the box), the same sign in the five scripts of the homes the parcels went to, and the legend of the four series that follow.

posts.caption:
Is it gold? It's 18k gold tone plated, and we'll always say so.

Dhanteras is for bringing home something new in metal. If it's these, here is the whole slip: Woven Gold Hoops, 25 mm across, a braided rope, no stones. ₹1,299. The pair our customers have ordered most since August.

[ woven gold hoops · 18k gold tone plated · told straight ]
posts.alt_text: A lilac tile. Large text asks: Is it gold? and answers: it's 18k gold tone plated, the slip will always say so. Below, a tailor's order slip lists Woven Gold Hoops, 25 mm across, no stones, 18k gold tone plated, solid gold: no, price 1,299 rupees. A pair of braided gold-tone hoops lies on a cream measuring tape marked at 25 mm.
posts.why: Dhanteras is Fri 6 Nov and the category spends it shouting 'Buy 1 Get 1 | 18K Gold' (Elra, live ad library). Naira's evidence says honesty wins: Tyaani runs 0% discount copy and holds the best-ranked creative of 498; the owner's own favourite lines are the honest ones ('is it real gold? NO.', 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald'); physical-proof framing ('THE WIDTH.' with calipers) pulled above-average ATC, and 'finished to be seen up close' beat 'daily wear' 3.8 to 2.2 ATC per ₹1k. Woven Gold Hoops is the #1 seller by units (20 in 120 days), 63 in stock, market score 9, and '25 mm, braided, no stones' is its proven fact. Friday 18:30 is inside the 18:00-21:00 order peak. Mid-weight tile between the loud kandil and the quiet Bhaubeej tile.
posts.claims_check: Woven Gold Hoops tags: 18k Gold Tone Plated, Earrings, Hypoallergenic, Tarnish Free, Waterproof. On the art: '18k gold tone plated' (tag), 'solid gold? no.' (true, and not a statement about plating content), '25 mm', 'braided', 'no stones' (proven ad facts). Slide 4 quotes the listing's tags as 'listed as' and adds the site FAQ's own caution (remove before swimming), so the water claim is never stronger than the brand's. No 'buy gold' framing: the caption says 'something new in metal'. 'Ordered most since August' = Shopify units (#1, 20 units, line live since early Aug). No base-metal words, no 'handmade'.

posts.alt_text: A deep bottle-green night tile. A glowing paper star lantern in aqua, pink and pale yellow hangs from a gold string, its paper tails trailing down toward a silver-tone bracelet of aqua, pink and pale yellow cushion stones, each in a halo. Text reads Shubh Deepavali in Devanagari, then: The kandil stays up all month. So can this.
posts.why: Diwali is Sun 8 Nov (Drik) and Sunday 12:00 is the top order slot. Prism Rivière is #1 by revenue (₹27,649 in 120 days), 67 in stock, and was the best static the account ever ran with its own story (49 ATC at ₹115); its pastels are literally kandil colours, already proven in the owner-approved Stories ('Diya, meet your match.', 'Still lit.'). The akash kandil is the Maharashtrian Diwali object and 46% of buyers are in Maharashtra. The research gap 'nobody decouples festive from red-and-gold' is answered with pastel on green. 'Stays up all month' keeps the tile alive into the wedding fortnight instead of expiring on the 9th. LOUD tile of row 3, dark over the light ivory P3.
posts.claims_check: Prism Rivière tags: Bracelet, Cubic Zirconia, Hypoallergenic, Rhodium Plated, Tarnish Free, Waterproof. No 'made to stay gold' (rhodium piece), no 'silver' as metal, no gold words. Cultural line softened in the caption ('in a lot of homes ... through Kartik'): owner to confirm the custom reads true to her. Velista never sets RIVIÈRE (no accented glyphs): the name is in Jost. One Indian cue (the kandil).

risks: Multi-script signboard (P1 slide 4) and every Devanagari line (मॅचिंग सेंटर, मैचिंग सेंटर, माप, शुभ दीपावली) must be checked glyph by glyph by native readers (Marathi, Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu) before posting; Tiro Kannada / Tamil / Telugu come from Google Fonts. If a script cannot be verified, drop that board rather than guess. Tiro Devanagari is a feed option, not yet a brand face: owner sign-off needed.

The WhatsApp 'send a photo, get three matches with photographs' promise (P1, P3, P8, P11, P12) extends the site's existing gifting line to outfit photos. The owner must confirm the team can answer these Mon-Sat 10-7 through the festive fortnight; if not, soften to the site's exact wording ('Tell us who it is for and your budget...').

Ruby stock velocity: Ruby bracelet 12 and Ruby huggies 12 against ~0.9 Ruby bracelets sold a day since 16 Oct. P1, P8 and P12 depend on them; check stock the evening before each and switch to Crystal (29 / 15) if a Ruby variant is at 5 or fewer. Never post a piece at 1-3 units.

'IS IT GOLD?' on Dhanteras (P5) is deliberately honest and could be misread at thumbnail size as a claim. The answer sits directly under it at 48px; if the owner is uncomfortable, the fallback headline is 'TOLD STRAIGHT.' with the same slip.

Cultural lines need the owner's eye: the akash kandil 'stays up all month' (P6, softened to 'in a lot of homes' in the caption) and the Tulsi Vivah joke (P11, no product near the plant). Both are affectionate, but they touch practice and ritual.

The shade tag puts the stand-alone blush flower (26px) on nine covers. Paid creative restricts the flower to a 6-15% ghost; in the feed it is a maker's mark on a hang-tag, never beside the wordmark. Owner call.

Matching Centre is a humble Indian institution; executed loosely (stickers, clutter, cheap textures, handwriting fonts) it reads down-market. What keeps it premium is the discipline in this spec: one piece per frame, real photography only, the raw-silk texture, gold hairlines, Velista + Cormorant, no stamps. Do not add props.
Three AI textile textures (silk, Paithani, sequins) must not read AI-made; if any does, replace with the flat SVG swatch (device 2) in the same colour. Never generate jewellery.
About 14 new BiRefNet cut-outs are needed (CUT-02 to CUT-12); the fine chains (Ribbon Bead, Marquise) and pavé edges need a hand check on the dark grounds, where a plaster halo shows.
Edition Two copy carries no water claims (house rule); only P5 quotes 'listed as waterproof', and adds the site FAQ's own 'take them off to swim'. Keep that pairing if the slide is edited.

Reels (P7, P10) must use Meta's Sound Collection (business account; labels have sued Indian brands over Reels music). If the owner prefers real footage for P10, the approved Kinn Films 'I asked for one photo' elegant cut can replace it with the same cover, but only as a Collab with the creator's written consent and without lyrics.

Posting natively in the Instagram app keeps 3:4; a scheduler may force 4:5. Every critical element sits inside y 45-1395, but test one draft through the scheduler first. Reel covers may not be editable after posting: upload the designed cover at publish time.
No pins during the rollout, and post strictly in order P1 to P12 (three a week) so each week completes one row; if a post slips, use grid reordering rather than doubling up on a day.
